summary: A seeded percent condition's outcome depends on the installation id, which the SDK draws at random in every context: production's context two fell to the default in pass 1 and inside the half in pass 2. Fireemu evaluates percent with the server template's hash (SHA-256 of <seed>.<installation id>); production's client hash was not recorded, so the outcome for a given id is not claimed.

The fetch tag has production's form, etag-<project>-firebase-fetch-<signed 32-bit number>, repeats for the same answer and changes with every version (as recorded); its number is a hash whose input production did not show, so fireemu's number differs.
Production answered the fetch and the stream gzip-encoded (content-encoding: gzip); fireemu answers them uncompressed. The decoded bodies are compared.
Production's answers carry vary: Origin, X-Origin, Referer; fireemu omits Vary without an Origin header and sends vary: origin when CORS applies.

Fireemu has no Installations service: the local comparison answers the SDK's Installations requests in the browser harness (coordinator ruling 10), so only the SDK's own requests are compared, not the answers.
